title: Serial Cell-free DNA Assessments in Preclinical Models
protocol: Seed human cancer cell lines into 96-well plates prior to treatment.
Use black 96-well clear bottom plates for measuring cell viability.
Use white 96-well clear bottom plates for measuring caspase activity.
Ensure the same 96-well plate is used for assessing cell viability, caspase activity, and media collection.
Include replicates of a media-only control condition in the experiment.
Prepare cultured cells according to their growth requirements.
Aspirate media from cells.
Wash cells with 5–10 mL of sterile 1× PBS.
Add 2 mL 0.25% Trypsin (2 mL per 10 cm plate).
Place the plates in a 37°C incubator and wait for cells to detach (~5 min).
Add 5–10 mL fresh media into trypsinized cells.
Transfer total volume into 15 mL falcon tube.
Centrifuge at 4°C, 5 min, 300 × g.
Aspirate media from the cells.
Resuspend cells in fresh media, adjusting volume based on confluency (e.g., 5 mL for 70% confluency).
Count total viable cells using Trypan Blue.
Determine the number of cells to seed per condition in a final volume of 200 μL per well.
Seed control wells with 500–1,000 cells optimally.
Seed treated wells with 8,000–12,000 cells optimally.
Ensure sufficient cell numbers for biological replicates and seeding errors by calculating an excess of 10%–20%.
Seed cells into wells of a 96-well plate using an 8-channel multichannel pipette.
Exclude outer wells to avoid edge effects.
Include 3–4 wells of media only as blank controls.
Fill unused wells with 200 μL of 1× PBS.
Place the 96-well plates into a 37°C incubator.
Allow cells to adhere for approximately 2 hours.
Proceed with treatment after cells are fully adhered.
If treating with IR, minimize time plates are removed from the 37°C incubator.
Remove unirradiated plates from the incubator for the same amount of time as irradiated plates.
For drug treatments, remove an equivalent volume of media to ensure the drug volume does not exceed 200 μL.
Add small volumes (10 μL or less) without removing media.
Remove and discard 20 μL of media from each well of the 96-well plate.
Add 20 μL of Presto Blue reagent using an 8-channel multichannel pipette into the corresponding wells of the same plate.
Return 96-well plates to 37°C incubator and incubate for 1 h.
Remove aliquot of CaspaseGlo® 3/7 reagent, wrap in aluminum foil to avoid exposure to light and allow to warm to 20°C–25°C.
Read fluorescence on plate reader set to 37°C using the following settings: Excitation (540–570 nm) and Emission (580–610 nm).
Set the plate reader temperature to 20°C–25°C after reading is complete.
Centrifuge 96-well plate at 4°C, 5 min, 200 × g.
Transfer 150 μL of media containing cfDNA from the centrifuged 96-well plate to pre-labeled 8-strip PCR tubes.
Store PCR tubes at −20°C until ready for downstream analysis.
Add 50 μL of CaspaseGlo® 3/7 reagent to each well of the 96-well plate.
Mix contents of wells gently using a plate shaker at 0.3 × g for 30 seconds.
Incubate the plate at 20°C–25°C for 1 hour.
Read luminescence on a plate reader as directed by the luminometer manufacturer.
Remove media samples from −20°C freezer.
Place samples on ice to thaw.
Label 8-strip PCR tubes.
Add 148.5 μL of DNA suspension buffer to each tube using an 8-channel multichannel pipette.
Vortex well and quick spin the thawed samples to remove media from the lid.
Add 1.5 μL of sample to pre-labeled tubes using an 8-channel multichannel pipette.
Ensure tips are changed to avoid cross contamination.
Store diluted samples at −20°C until ready to quantify cfDNA.
Aspirate media from cancer cell lines and resuspend in fresh media based on confluency (e.g., 5 mL for cells at 70% confluency).
Count the total number of viable cells suspended in media using Trypan Blue.
Determine the number of cells to inject per mouse, typically between 150,000 and 5 × 10^6 cells per mouse.
Transfer the required volume of cell suspension to a new falcon tube.
Centrifuge the total volume of cell suspension at 4°C for 5 minutes at 200 x g.
Prepare cold Matrigel at a 1:4 ratio with cold 1× PBS.
Aspirate the media and resuspend cells in cold Matrigel-1X PBS solution for all mice in one tube.
Mix the cell/Matrigel mixture well by tapping the tube and/or inverting it.
Keep the cell/Matrigel mixture on ice immediately before injections.
Fill the syringe with cell/Matrigel mixture when the mice are ready to be injected.
Hold the mouse in an Intraperitoneal (IP) hold.
Subcutaneously inject 100 μL of cell/Matrigel mixture into the right or left flank of each mouse.
Monitor tumor growth by palpation and caliper measurements.
Measure the length, width, and height of each tumor using calipers.
Randomize mice into treatment groups (5-10 mice per group).
Collect an aliquot of blood before irradiation for pre-treatment baseline.
Irradiate tumors according to the guidelines of the irradiator.
Deliver a dose of 20 Gy using an IGRT-XRAD 225Cs irradiator, half from the top and half from the bottom of the tumor.
Use integrated software and cone-beam computed tomography volume scans for targeting the desired irradiation area.
Perform irradiations at 225 kVp and 13 mA.
Wear a surgical mask when handling blood samples and processing plasma.
Label Microvette CB 300 tubes coated with EDTA with corresponding mouse IDs.
Place a sterile 5 mm lancet on a paper towel within a laminar flow hood.
Open tubes and have gauze pads nearby for easy access.
Prepare 1 ml syringes with attached needle containing 150 μl of saline per mouse.
Reconstrain the animal using the scruffing technique.
Minimize side-to-side movement of the head during venipuncture.
Visualize the hair whorl or hairless dimple along the curvature of the mandible.
Locate the submandibular vein in the groove past the jawbone.
Hold the lancet perpendicular to the bleed site.
Apply firm pressure with the point of the lancet caudal to the eye and ventral to the ear where the submandibular vein is located.
Release the pressure until blood flows.
Place the blood collection tube below the puncture site to collect 2–3 drops (50–100 μL).
Place the collected blood on ice.
Process the blood within 1 h of collection.
Apply gentle pressure with gauze until bleeding has stopped.
Inject 150 μL of saline IP to ensure hydration of mouse for subsequent blood draws.
Centrifuge blood samples at 2,500 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Pre-label 1.5 mL microtubes using a label maker for plasma and blood pellet before blood processing.
Label two tubes per sample: one for plasma and one for the blood pellet.
Transfer separated plasma portion to a clean 1.5 mL microtube labeled blood pellet.
Keep remaining blood portion on ice.
Centrifuge new tubes with collected plasma at 16,100 × g for 10 min at 4°C to remove additional debris.
Record and transfer entire volume of plasma to the new microtube labeled plasma.
Record plasma volume on the side of the tube and in a lab book.
Transfer remaining blood pellet to the corresponding microtube tubes labeled blood pellet if desired.
Store all tubes at −80°C.
Wear a mask when handling samples to avoid contamination from human DNA.
Prepare a solution of 1× Phosphate Buffer Solution + 0.5 mM EDTA to top up plasma samples to a total volume of 200 μL.
Print out a sheet with sample IDs, plasma volumes, and required top-up volumes to 200 μL.
Print out the layout of samples in a 96-well format.
Wear a surgical mask when purifying plasma samples.
Set oven to 60°C.
Remove plasma samples from −80°C and thaw on ice.
Add 20 μL of proteinase K to the bottom of each collection microtube.
Top up plasma samples to 200 μL with 1× PBS + 0.5 mM EDTA solution if required.
Place samples in a microtube rack at 20°C–25°C.
Label tubes 1–8, 9–16 etc., to maintain sample order.
Transfer the entire volume of plasma samples (200 μL) to each corresponding collection microtube carefully near the bottom.
Pipette 200 μL of buffer ACL (without RNAse carrier) using an 8-channel multichannel pipette.
Cap the tubes carefully and apply plastic cling wrap to avoid spilling.
Vortex each strip for 15 s, pulsing.
Keep your hand on the top of the tubes to ensure the caps do not come off.
Remove the plastic cling wrap carefully and place the collection microtubes back in the rack.
Balance the rack and centrifuge at the highest speed (3,468 × g) for 1 min to collect any solution from the caps.
Weigh the tube rack on a scale and adjust for balance with water.
Wrap each strip of collection microtubes in plastic cling wrap after centrifugation.
Place the wrapped tubes in the 60°C oven to incubate for 30 min.
Turn the oven temperature to 56°C.
Carefully uncap the tubes, placing the caps upwards to avoid contamination.
Pipette 200 μL of ACB buffer using an 8-channel multichannel pipette.
Repeat steps involving weighing and balancing as necessary.
Place tubes on ice for 5 min immediately after vortexing.
Ensure accurate balancing by weighing the tube rack on a scale and adjusting for balance with water.
Set up the 96-well Vacuum Manifold (use NucleoVac 96 Vacuum Manifold with Square-block spacer).
Insert appropriate spacers in the manifold base.
Place an S-block on top to collect waste.
Place the manifold lid on top of the manifold base.
Place the QIAamp 96 plate on top of the manifold lid.
Cover unused wells on the QIAamp 96 plate with a plastic seal if present.
Apply the entire mixture (620 μL per collection microtube) to the QIAamp 96 plate for each sample.
Carefully remove the caps from the tubes to avoid cross contamination.
Use a P1000 to transfer samples to the plate initially.
Switch to a P200 to transfer any residual sample.
Begin drawing up the samples when pipette tips contact the liquid, avoiding overflow by lowering tips carefully into the tube.
Seal the QIAamp 96 plate with an AirPore Tape sheet.
Turn on the vacuum and allow sample to flow through the column for binding.
Remove the QIAamp 96 plate from the manifold.
Place the QIAamp 96 plate between two tip boxes to avoid contamination of samples.
Empty the flow-through waste in the S-block using an aspirator.
Return the QIAmp 96 plate to the manifold.
Add 500 μL Buffer AW1 using an 8-channel multichannel pipette to each well.
Weigh the QIAamp 96 plate/S-block and adjust the balance.
Centrifuge at 3,468 × g for 10 minutes.
Remove the QIAamp 96 plate from the S-block.
Place the QIAmp 96 plate between two tip boxes.
Incubate in the oven at 56°C for 10 minutes.
Ensure there is enough space in the oven and prepare two tip boxes to balance the QIAamp 96 plate without touching the bottom of the plate.
Place the QIAamp 96 plate directly on top a rack of elution microtubes.
Add 100 μL of EB buffer at 20°C–25°C using an 8-channel multichannel pipette to each well of the QIAamp 96 plate.
Seal the QIAamp 96 plate with a new AirPore Tape sheet and incubate for 10 min at 20°C–25°C.
Weigh the QIAamp 96 plate/rack of elution microtubes and adjust the balance.
Centrifuge at the highest speed (our centrifuge was set to 3,468 × g) for 12 min.
Transfer the entire volume from each elution microtube into new labeled tubes.
Store purified cfDNA samples at −20°C.
Pre-label tubes ahead of time.
Transfer samples to the appropriate pre-labeled tubes.
Use a printed layout to ensure accuracy in positioning each sample on the QIAamp 96 plate.
Quantify cell-free DNA by qPCR targeting human LINE-1 (hLINE-1).
Set up qPCR reactions in a qPCR hood to avoid contamination of human DNA.
Make a human genomic standard dilution series ahead of time.
Use the same material for all standard curves when comparing multiple qPCR plates.
Aliquot each dilution into 8-strip PCR tubes and store at −20°C.
Ensure each aliquot has enough material for three technical replicates of 4 μL each + 20%–30% of total volume.
Prepare a 5-step 10-fold dilution series between 0.0125 pg/μL and 125 pg/μL.
Prepare genomic standards in DNA suspension buffer for diluted media samples.
Prepare genomic standards in EB buffer for purified plasma cfDNA samples.
Use two nested hLINE-1 primer sets to quantify cfDNA.
Amplify fragments 82 base pairs or larger with the short hLINE-1 primer set.
Amplify fragments 224 base pairs or larger with the long hLINE-1 primer set.
Calculate an integrity index as the ratio of long hLINE-1/short hLINE-1.
Thaw diluted cell line media samples or purified plasma cfDNA samples on ice.
Prepare a working stock of hLINE-1 primer pair by adding forward and reverse primers to achieve a final concentration of 2.5 μM in MQ water.
Mix the hLINE-1 primer stock well by vortexing.
Make a master mix of SYBR Green supermix to hLINE-1 primer working stock at a ratio of 5:1 for the number of desired reactions plus 10%.
Vortex the thawed diluted samples and SYBR Green-hLINE-1 primer master mix to ensure they are well mixed.
Place an ice box with a Kim wipe on top in the qPCR hood.
Prepare a 384-well plate by marking which wells will be used.
Add 6 μL of the SYBR Green-hLINE-1 primer master mix to designated wells of the 384-well plate.
Add 4 μL of each purified plasma or diluted cell line media sample to the wells of the 384-well plate.
Hover the pipette tip over the wells and carefully dispense the sample onto the side of the well.
Create the genomic standard curve by adding 4 μL of the 10-fold genomic standard dilution series to the wells of the 384-well plate.
Mix the standards well by flicking tubes gently.
Fill three wells with DNA suspension buffer as a no template control (NTC).
Seal the plate properly with a seal compatible with qPCR.
Check the seal for damage or dirty spots before proceeding.
Centrifuge the plate briefly for 1 min at 200 × g to ensure all material is at the bottom of the well.
Run the qPCR using an appropriate program.
Ensure the standard curve has a R2 value >0.9.
Ensure sample Cq values fall before the NTC (above background).
Export data to the format of choice, such as an excel file.
Calculate starting quantities (SQs) for all reactions using the corresponding standard curve.
Divide SQ by the sample input volume (4 μL).
Multiply SQs by the dilution factor if any (e.g., 100 X).
Average the SQ of each sample by averaging replicates.
Remove a clear single outlier to get a more accurate estimate of the SQ if necessary.
Normalize and calculate the final cfDNA concentration for each sample.
For diluted media samples, normalize cfDNA concentrations by the initial seeding density.
If the same seeding density was used for all conditions, omit normalization step.
Average the normalized cfDNA concentration of biological replicates of control samples.
Calculate fold change in cfDNA release by dividing normalized cfDNA concentration from treated samples to corresponding averaged control samples.
Calculate the absolute cfDNA concentration using the equation C = Q × VDNA/VqPCR × 1/Vext.
Determine the starting quantity Q by qPCR.
Use a total volume of DNA obtained after extraction, approximately 85 μL.
Measure the volume of DNA solution used for qPCR, which is 4 μL.
Record the volume of plasma extracted.
Normalize cfDNA concentrations to tumor volume at each timepoint.
Derive "cfDNA density" by comparing Pre-irradiation (0 h) values at all time points.
